1.title: Governance and Compliance for AI
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Governance and Compliance for A I. This module covers task statement five point two, and closes the content of the exam guide. You will learn which A W S services support governance and compliance, how to govern data, and which processes keep A I systems under review. The exam gives you an audit need and asks you to name the service or process.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Identify the A W S services that support governance and compliance: Config, Inspector, Artifact, CloudTrail and Trusted Advisor. Describe data governance strategies: lifecycles, logging, residency, monitoring and retention. And describe governance processes: policies, review cadence, frameworks such as the Generative A I Security Scoping Matrix, transparency standards and training.

1.title: Case Check-In: Cedar and Salt Meets the Auditors
1.text: At Cedar and Salt Travel, auditors ask for proof of compliance for the booking assistant. Their questions: what rules apply, what is configured, who did what, and how long do we keep guest data? Leaders want a repeatable review, not a one-time check. Your job is to choose the services and the processes.

1.title: The Regulatory Landscape and AWS Compliance
1.text: First, the regulatory landscape. A I-specific rules and frameworks include the E U A I Act and the N I S T A I Risk Management Framework. Data protection laws include G D P R, and C C P A and C P R A. Industry rules include H I P A A for health, and A P R A for finance. Cross-border data needs data sovereignty controls. A W S has an accredited I S O I E C forty-two thousand and one certification for A I services; the certificate lists the covered services and is in A W S Artifact. But that does not make your application compliant; you still must comply. As of five November twenty twenty-six, check the A W S compliance pages for current scope. Exam tip: A W S provides compliant infrastructure, and you prove your own application complies.

1.title: AWS Config and Amazon Inspector
1.text: Two services check your own environment. A W S Config records how resources are configured and how they changed. It evaluates them with rules and conformance packs. Use it to show that settings follow policy, such as encrypted buckets, and to keep configuration history for audits. Amazon Inspector continuously scans E C two instances, container images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and network exposure. Use it to find and fix weaknesses in the workloads that run your A I application. Exam tip: configuration history and rules mean A W S Config, and vulnerability scanning means Amazon Inspector.

1.title: AWS Artifact, AWS CloudTrail and AWS Trusted Advisor
1.text: Three more services matter. A W S Artifact gives on-demand A W S compliance reports, such as S O C, I S O and P C I, plus online agreements. A W S CloudTrail records who did what, and when, as events. You get ninety days of event history free, trails that deliver to S three, and CloudTrail Lake for longer retention. A W S Trusted Advisor checks your environment against best practices and recommends fixes. As of five November twenty twenty-six, the full set of Trusted Advisor checks needs a paid support plan, and the plan names are changing. Exam tip: reports for auditors is Artifact, activity history is CloudTrail, and best-practice checks is Trusted Advisor.

1.title: Data Governance Strategies
1.text: Data governance has five strategies. Data lifecycle: define how data is collected, used, archived and deleted. Logging: keep audit trails of data access and model interactions. Residency: keep data in approved Regions, and control cross-border use. Monitoring and observation: watch data use, quality and drift, with alerts. And retention: keep records as long as the rules require, and no longer. Exam tip: name the data question first. How long, where, who, and what changed?

1.title: AWS Services for Data Governance
1.text: Several A W S services support data governance. A W S Lake Formation is one place for fine-grained access control to data lakes, down to columns, rows and cells, with audit logs in CloudTrail. Amazon S three Glacier storage classes give low-cost, long-term archives for data you must retain, and S three lifecycle rules move data between classes. Amazon Bedrock data retention lets you control whether prompts and outputs are retained, per Region, with modes such as none, default and A W S review. Region choice keeps data resident where the rules require. As of five November twenty twenty-six, retention modes apply to specific models, so check the model's terms. Exam tip: data lake permissions mean Lake Formation, and cheap long-term retention means S three Glacier.

1.title: Governance Processes
1.text: Governance is also about processes. Policies are written rules for acceptable A I use, data and risk limits. A review cadence means regular reviews and updates, not a one-time approval. Review strategies use a multidisciplinary team of legal, security, ethics, business and technical people, plus an A I risk register and audits. Transparency standards mean you disclose A I use and document models and data. And team training means people learn the policies, the risks and responsible use. Exam tip: governance is a cycle of policy, review, audit and training.

1.title: The Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix
1.text: The Generative A I Security Scoping Matrix has five scopes. The picture shows them as steps. Scope one: use a public generative A I service. Scope two: use an enterprise application with embedded generative A I. Scope three: build on a pre-trained model through an A P I. Scope four: fine-tune a model with your data. Scope five: train a model from scratch. The more you own of the model and data, the more responsibility you take on. The matrix also names five disciplines: governance and compliance, legal and privacy, risk management, controls, and resilience. Exam tip: the more you own, the more governance work falls to you.

1.title: What the Exam Asks: Governance and Compliance
1.text: Here is how the exam frames this module. Which service: Config, Inspector, Artifact, CloudTrail or Trusted Advisor. Which data strategy: lifecycle, logging, residency, monitoring or retention. Which process: policies, review cadence, review strategy, transparency standard or training. Which framework: the Generative A I Security Scoping Matrix, and which scope. And which regulation: the E U A I Act, N I S T, G D P R, H I P A A or I S O I E C forty-two thousand and one. Exam tip: name the need first. Report, history, scan, configuration or rule?

1.title: Design Check: Cedar and Salt Meets the Auditors
1.text: Now a design check. Cover the right column and name the answer. A copy of A W S's I S O and S O C reports: A W S Artifact. Who called the model A P I s, and when: A W S CloudTrail. Proof that buckets stay encrypted, with history: A W S Config rules. Are our compute workloads free of known vulnerabilities: Amazon Inspector. A quick best-practice check of the account: A W S Trusted Advisor. Column-level access to guest data in the data lake: A W S Lake Formation. Keep old logs for years, cheaply: S three Glacier classes. And a booking app that uses a third-party model through an A P I: Scope three of the scoping matrix. Pause the video if you want more time.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. The services are Config, Inspector, Artifact, CloudTrail and Trusted Advisor. Data governance covers lifecycle, logging, residency, monitoring and retention, with Lake Formation and S three Glacier. The processes are policies, review cadence, review strategies, transparency standards and training. The framework is the Generative A I Security Scoping Matrix, with five scopes. And on regulation, A W S certifications do not make you compliant.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which A W S service provides on-demand downloads of A W S compliance reports, such as S O C and I S O reports? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A W S Artifact. It gives on-demand access to A W S security and compliance documents and agreements. Config records configurations, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, and Trusted Advisor checks best practices.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Cedar and Salt must show auditors who called its Amazon Bedrock A P I s and when. Which service records this activity? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A W S CloudTrail. It records actions taken by a user, role or A W S service as events, so you can see who did what and when. Config tracks resource configuration, and Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Select two. Which two statements about A W S Config and Amazon Inspector are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C. Config records resource configurations and evaluates them against rules. Inspector continuously scans E C two instances, container images and Lambda functions for vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. A P I activity is CloudTrail, and toxic content is handled by Guardrails.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Cedar and Salt builds its assistant on a third-party pre-trained foundation model through an A P I. Which scope of the Generative A I Security Scoping Matrix fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Scope three, pre-trained models. Scope four refines a model with your data, and Scope five trains a model from scratch.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which approach best supports governance of an A I system over time? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: regular reviews, an A I risk register, audits and team training. Governance is a repeating cycle. A one-time approval, or untrained and unreviewed rules, cannot keep pace with change.

1.title: Answers at a Glance
1.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: A. Question two: C. Question three: A and C. Question four: B. Question five: D. That completes the fourteen content modules. Next, Module fifteen is a quick-reference recap and service chooser for the whole exam.
